cases.native_source: function applyDiscount(amount, percent) { return amount - Math.round(amount * percent / 100); }
cases.reference_body: if !(percent >= 0 && percent <= 100) { Parsed { ok: false, value: 0 } } else { Parsed { ok: true, value: amount - amount * percent / 100 } }
cases.fixed_reference_body: if !(percent >= 0 && percent <= 100) { Parsed { ok: false, value: 0 } } else { Parsed { ok: true, value: amount - amount * percent / 100 } }
cases.candidate_body: if percent < 0 || percent > 100 { Parsed { ok: false, value: 0 } } else { let roundedDiscount = (amount * percent + 50) / 100; Parsed { ok: true, value: amount - roundedDiscount } }
cases.rationale: Nearest-cent rounding is the source-like implementation of the Math.round abstraction. The one-cent tolerance classifies exact truncation differences as boundary-only inconclusive evidence rather than blocking them, while keeping larger differences visible. The syntactic success-flag warning may remain; boundary-only evidence does not itself confirm equality, so acceptance still requires independent replay evidence or an exact match.
